title: zoneinfo — IANA time zone support — Python 3.14.8 documentation
snippet: The zoneinfo module provides a concrete time zone implementation to support the IANA time zone database as originally specified in PEP 615. By default, zoneinfo uses the system’s time zone data if available; if no system time zone data is available, the library will fall back to using the first-party tzdata package available on PyPI.

title: Python zoneinfo Module - W3Schools
snippet: Definition and Usage The zoneinfo module provides support for IANA time zone database, allowing you to work with time zones in a standard and reliable way. Use it to convert between time zones, handle daylight saving time transitions, and work with historical time zone data.

snippet: The zoneinfo module, introduced in Python 3.9 under PEP 615, brings native support for the IANA (Internet Assigned Numbers Authority) time zone database directly into Python's standard library.

title: Python zoneinfo: Working with Time Zones Made Easy
snippet: Aug 8, 2026 · In Python, the zoneinfo module provides a powerful and straightforward way to handle time zones. It has been part of the standard library since Python 3.9 (PEP 615), and is now the recommended approach for time zone handling — replacing third-party libraries like pytz, which is in maintenance mode and offers no advantages on modern Python.

title: Time Zones - Internet Assigned Numbers Authority
snippet: Time Zones The Time Zone Database (often called tz or zoneinfo) contains code and data that represent the history of local time for many representative locations worldwide. It is updated periodically to reflect changes made by political bodies to time zone boundaries, UTC offsets, and daylight-saving rules. The database is primarily intended for software implementers.
